body:
REQUIRED BY §32's OWN CRITERION 11 (#257): the seam census found exactly one standing violation of rule R1 (every erasure-adjacent report verifiable at the bytes; unverifiable reads as not-done) and this ticket tracks it, created before the spec landed, as the criterion demands.

THE VIOLATION (`src/gateway/esm.ts:8-21`, per the census): a renderer/resolver module compiled from a source delta stays loaded and EXECUTABLE after that source delta is erased — the compiled module is a copy of the bytes living outside every tier `holds()` asks — while `health()` reports the erasure settled. Confessed only in code comments today, which is exactly the shape H7 forbids: the report can be false, and the confession is somewhere no operator reads.

TWO HALVES, different merge tiers per the standing erasure rule:
- (a) HONESTY, self-merge tier: `health()` (and the erase receipt's tier list) names loaded-module residency as an unproven tier rather than staying silent — refusing where it used to claim. Cheap, shippable first.
- (b) COMPLETION, repair tier: the erase fan-out tears down compiled modules whose source delta was condemned (registry eviction on the same pass that purges bytes), with the rail two-sided — the module is gone AND a named sibling module compiled from a live delta still serves. This completes a promise §11 already states rather than widening anything: no user data is touched, only the executable copy of what was already condemned.

CARE: teardown must not brick a serving route mid-request (the T31/mount discipline — a dropped world answers as if it never existed, not with a 500); and the census's own wording is the acceptance bar — after (a)+(b), §32's census row for ESM residency flips from VIOLATION to instance-of-R1, and the spec's landed text must be updated in the same PR or the census lies.

HALF-OVERTAKEN (stale sweep, 2026-08-25) — read this before building: Half (a) honesty died (landed): src/gateway/erase.ts:729 carries ESM_RESIDENCY_DISCLOSURE in health().nonSwept, and src/gateway/esm.ts:14-20 records 'T105 (a) named the tier honestly'. Half (b) completion lives: the ESM cache has no eviction — the same header defers teardown to 'T105 b' and names the closing rail (erase a resolver, loadedEsm undefined) as unbuilt.
title: ESM residency: erased source stays executable while health() reports settled — the tree's one standing R1 violation
